transcription: You're not lying. Are you? The building doesn't look like anything I hadn't seen before. Not broken down, not nice. Just kind of there. Like it forgot how to be noticed, not hidden just forgotten. A beige block with no balconies and windows that look more like shut eyes than glass. I double-check the address I printed, it's still crumpled in my coat pocket like it's holding something heavier than paper and stare up at it again. Four floors. But the listing said it was a third floor walk-up. Weird. I buzzed 3 billion nevertheless. No answer. I start to buzz again, but before I press the button, I hear the soft click of the door unlocking. No voice. No movement. It just opened. I took a deep long breath in, and against my better judgment I step in. The air inside doesn't smell like anything. That's the first thing I notice. Not clean, not musty, not like dust or fabric softener or mold. Just. Nothing. Even my shoes sound too loud on the hallway tile, like I'm walking through someone else's dream. The stairwell has no windows, and the walls are painted this weird gray. Not the kind from trendy magazines, the kind that lives in basements. I pass a small, fake plan on the landing. It's plastic. Dustless. 3 billion left The door is already cracked open. She's already sitting at the table. Lilith. She doesn't say hi at first. Just gestures for me to come in. Like this is a waiting room and I'm late for something I didn't know I signed up for. Her hair is pulled back so tight it makes my scalp ache just looking at her. She wears a gray sweater. Black slacks. Like she's heading to a funeral or court. I step in. She stands up and reaches out her hand with a small smile that feels. Efficient. Not warm. Not cold. Just like she's done at a hundred times and stopped caring around number 30. You're eating. That didn't feel like a question. Yeah. Thank you for being on time. I almost say I wasn't sure if I was supposed to knock, but stop myself. Instead, I nod. Lilith gestures to a white table in the kitchen, where two glasses of water sit untouched and a thick manila folder rests between them. She sits. I sit across her. She slides the folder toward me. This is the cohabitation agreement. It's a formality. Thuro, but not invasive. I open it. The first few pages are fine. Rent details, utilities, shared spaces. Then things start getting. Odd. Rule five. No mirrors in common areas. Rule nine blinds must be closed between 9.00p and 7.00a. Rule 11 you are required to keep a nightly journal. Proms will be provided. Rule 15 all lies must be recorded in the journal, no matter how small. I read that one three times. Wait, I say, all lies? Lilith meets my eyes and holds them too long. Lying is a form of self-harm, eaten. It doesn't sound like a metaphor. She says it the way people recite ingredients on a box of cookies. This is a place where you recover. She continues. Not regress. Recover from what? I didn't even want to ask. I don't remember telling her I needed to recover from anything. Maybe she sees something I don't. I turn the page. Rule 19 the stairwell to the fourth floor is not to be used. Rule 20 if the door to the fourth floor is found open. Do not enter. Close it immediately. Rule 21 do not speak to anyone who claims to live above you. My fingers pause. I thought there wasn't a fourth floor. That was the first of a million racing thoughts through my mind that came out audibly. There isn't. She says it instantly. Smoothly. Like a knife that's been sharpened for this exact sentence. Something tightens behind my ribs. A pressure, not quite pain. I look at the contract again. The letters don't blur, but they feel heavier now. Lilith hands me a pen. I'll make a copy one side. You'll get the original. I don't want to sign it. What choice do I really have? The bedroom is bare. A twin mattress, a small desk, and a closet with no door. One drawer, and a lamp. On the desk, my new journal is already waiting. It's open to the first page. A single line written in the top corner what did you lie about today? I stare at it. My fingers twitch. Did I lie today? I told Lilith I was excited to move in. That's not true. I told her I'm doing fine. That's not true either. I told her I quit smoking. I didn't. Not really planning on it with my current circumstances. I pick up the pen. I said I'm excited. I'm not. I'm scared. I close the journal and crawl into bed without changing. The sheets are stiff and smell like they've been washed a hundred times but never used. The pillow makes no sound. I try to fall asleep. S-K-R-R-R-R-R-R-R-R-R-K. I sit up. What the actual F was that? Another piercing screech ravaged my ears. Directly above me. A slow, dragging scrape. Like furniture being pulled across hardwood. No like something heavier. Something that shouldn't be moving at all. There's no one above me. I remember that. Lilith said this is the top floor. But the sound continues slow and deliberate. Scrape. Pause. Scrape. I get up and cross to the window. Feel the blind just a little. The air outside looks blue and still. Across the street, a woman smokes on her balcony. The building next door is taller. The sky above it is blank. No clouds. No movement. I look up.
